COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 149 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Ms. Geetanjali Dhami, learned 
counsel for the revisionist.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. 
along with Mrs. Sweta Badola Dobhal, 
learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. The instant criminal revision has 
been preferred by the revisionist
(convict)against the judgment and order
passed by the trial court convicting the 
revisionist for the offences punishable 
under Section 51(1-A) read with Section 
49-B of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972,
with the sentence of three years simple
imprisonment with the fine of Rs. 25,000/. 
The appellate court also affirmed the 
judgment. As per the office report the 
revision is well within time.
4. Admit.
5. Summon the Trial Court Record.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist 
submits that the revisionist has not 
surrendered and the exemption application 
has been moved on the ground that the 
father of the revisionist recently got
cardiac arrest and he is under regular 
treatment and furthermore, he was on bail 
during trial. 7. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A 
submits have not disputed this fact that 
the revisionist was on bail during trial.
8. After hearing the learned counsel for 
the parties and taking into consideration 
that revisionist was on bail during trial and 
his father is under regular treatment, the 
exemption application is allowed.
9. List this case in the in the week 
commencing 13.04.2026.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
27.02.2026
Nahid
